claim.text: For Excel's EVEN and ODD functions, Microsoft documents rounding away from zero to the nearest even or odd integer and #VALUE! for nonnumeric input. For ISEVEN and ISODD, Microsoft documents truncation before the parity check and #VALUE! for nonnumeric input; the general IS-functions guidance says these arguments are not converted. Formula Atlas records documented behavior separately from scalar coercion and range profiles that still need Excel verification.
claim.subject_definition: Microsoft Excel function references and a proposed Formula Atlas semantic glossary for EVEN, ODD, ISEVEN, and ISODD

source.excerpt: Microsoft Support pages retrieved 2026-09-24: EVEN and ODD each say values are rounded away from zero regardless of sign, already-matching integers remain unchanged, and nonnumeric values return #VALUE!. ISEVEN and ISODD say fractional parts are truncated before parity is tested and nonnumeric input returns #VALUE!. The IS-functions overview describes ISEVEN and ISODD as IS functions and says their shared argument is not converted.
source.subject_definition: Microsoft Excel 365 desktop documentation for EVEN, ODD, ISEVEN, ISODD, and the IS-functions group
